best_for: Developers who like VS Code but want an MIT-licensed build with telemetry off by default, and who can live without Microsoft's proprietary extensions.

points.title: Same editor, different build
points.text: VSCodium is built from the same MIT-licensed source as VS Code, without Microsoft's branding, license or telemetry. If you know VS Code, nothing new to learn.

points.title: Extensions come from Open VSX
points.text: Microsoft's Marketplace terms limit it to Microsoft products, so VSCodium uses the Open VSX registry by default.

points.title: Some Microsoft extensions will not work
points.text: The C# debugger, the Windows C++ debugger and the Remote Development extensions are licensed only for the official VS Code build. Workarounds exist for some, such as Samsung's netcoredbg for C#, but if you rely on the Remote Development extensions, stay with VS Code.

points.title: Telemetry off, with limits
points.text: VSCodium turns off VS Code's telemetry, crash reporting and experiments. Extensions can still send their own telemetry, and update checks stay on unless you change `update.mode`.

points.title: Flatpak is from the team
points.text: The Flathub build is verified as published by the VSCodium team, for x64 and ARM64. Its .deb and .rpm repositories are run by a third party.

points.title: Install per user or for all
points.text: Windows gets user and machine installers for x64 and ARM64, and this site keeps 200 Windows versions. macOS comes as Intel and Apple silicon zips; macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
